title: Complementary components of a reduced pure subcurve
statement: Let $X$ be a reduced Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover). Suppose every irreducible component of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] has topological Krull dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $Y\subseteq X$ be a reduced closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] all of whose irreducible components have dimension $1$. Let $Z\subseteq X$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{|X|\setminus|Y|}$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. There is a subset $I$ of the finite set of irreducible components of $X$ such that $Y$ is the reduced closed union of the components in $I$ and $Z$ is the reduced closed union of all remaining components. Every irreducible component of $Z$ has dimension $1$, and the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{|X|\setminus|Z|}$ is $Y$. Empty $Y$ and empty $Z$ are allowed; the component dimension condition for the empty scheme is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), first paragraph of the proof: reduced equidimensional one-dimensional closed subschemes are unions of components; the complementary-union and double-complement consequences require no nodal hypothesis.

proof.text: The irreducible components of the Noetherian scheme $X$ form a finite set by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. If $X$ is empty, take $I=\varnothing$; then $Y$ and $Z$ are empty and all assertions are vacuous. Assume henceforth that $X$ is nonempty. Every point of $X$ lies on an irreducible component by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover].

source.place: Tag 0E38 first paragraph, with the Noetherian component-finiteness input

proof.text: Let $C$ be an irreducible component of $Y$. It is a closed irreducible subset of $X$, and by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] it is contained in an irreducible component $D$ of $X$. If $C\subsetneq D$, then $U=D\setminus C$ is a nonempty open subset of the irreducible space $D$. Apply [new-node-irreducible-open-complement-dimension] to $D$, with $d=1$ and this $U$. Since $D$ has dimension $1$, the result gives an integer $e<1$ with $\dim C\le e$, hence $\dim C\le0$. This contradicts the hypothesis that every irreducible component of $Y$ has dimension $1$. Therefore $C=D$ is an irreducible component of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 first paragraph: a reduced equidimensional one-dimensional closed subscheme is a union of irreducible components

proof.text: Let $I$ be the subset of the finite component set of $X$ consisting of those components that occur as a component $C$ of $Y$ in Step 2. Every point of $Y$ lies on a component of $Y$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] applied to the underlying space of $Y$, and Step 2 identifies that component with a member of $I$. Conversely every member of $I$ is contained in $Y$. Thus $|Y|$ is exactly the union of the components in $I$. Because $Y$ is reduced and is a closed subscheme with this support, uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies $Y$ with the reduced closed union of those components.

source.place: Tag 0E38 first paragraph and the reduced-induced uniqueness statement

proof.text: Let $J$ be the complementary subset of the finite component set of $X$, and let $W=\bigcup_{D\in J}|D|$. This is closed. If $x\in|X|\setminus|Y|$, choose an irreducible component $D$ containing $x$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. It cannot lie in $I$, because every component in $I$ is contained in $Y$; hence $x\in W$. Thus $|X|\setminus|Y|\subseteq W$ and its closure is contained in $W$. Conversely, for $D\in J$, let $\eta_D$ be its generic point from [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. If $\eta_D\in|Y|$, the closedness of $Y$ would imply $D=\overline{\{\eta_D\}}\subseteq|Y|$, which is impossible: by Step 3, $|Y|=\bigcup_{C\in I}C$, so irreducibility of $D$ forces $D$ into one selected $C$ (repeatedly apply the two-closed-set definition to this finite union); maximality of components then gives $D=C\in I$. Hence $\eta_D\in|X|\setminus|Y|$, and $D=\overline{\{\eta_D\}}$ is contained in the closure of $|X|\setminus|Y|$. Taking the finite union over $J$ gives $W=\overline{|X|\setminus|Y|}$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), first paragraph, with the finite-component closure argument written out; Tags 004W (lemma-irreducible) and 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: By definition, $Z$ is the reduced induced closed subscheme on $W$. The irreducible components of the finite union $W=\bigcup_{D\in J}D$ are exactly the members of $J$: if $E$ is irreducible in $W$, the finite closed cover $E=\bigcup_{D\in J}(E\cap D)$ forces $E\subseteq D$ for one $D$, by repeated use of the two-closed-set definition. Each $D\in J$ is itself irreducible and closed in $W$, and no one contains another by maximality in $X$. Thus the maximal irreducible subsets of $W$ are precisely these $D$. Therefore every irreducible component of $Z$ has dimension $1$, and $Z$ is the reduced closed union of all components of $X$ not in $I$. If $J=\varnothing$, then $W$ and $Z$ are empty and this conclusion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), first paragraph, with the finite-component closure argument written out; Tags 004W (lemma-irreducible) and 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: Put $V=|X|\setminus|Z|=|X|\setminus W$. Every $x\in V$ lies on a component of $X$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], and that component must be in $I$ because each component in $J$ lies in $W$. Thus $V\subseteq|Y|$, so $\overline V\subseteq|Y|$ since $Y$ is closed. Conversely, for $D\in I$, take its generic point $\eta_D$ from [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. If $\eta_D\in W$, then $\eta_D\in C$ for some $C\in J$; closedness of $C$ gives $D=\overline{\{\eta_D\}}\subseteq C$, and maximality of components gives $D=C$, contradicting $I\cap J=\varnothing$. Hence $\eta_D\in V$ and $D\subseteq\overline V$. The union over $I$ gives $|Y|\subseteq\overline V$, proving $\overline{|X|\setminus|Z|}=|Y|$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] now identifies the reduced induced closed subscheme on this support with $Y$. The argument includes $I=\varnothing$ and $J=\varnothing$, so both empty-complement cases are covered.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), first paragraph, with the finite-component closure argument written out; Tags 004W (lemma-irreducible) and 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

lean.statement: theorem complementary_pure_subcurve_components {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X] [IsNoetherian X] (hX : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, topologicalKrullDim C = 1) (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsReduced Y] (hY : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Y, topologicalKrullDim C = 1) (j : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] [IsReduced Z] (hZ : Set.range j = closure ((Set.range i)ᶜ)) : ∃ I : Set (Set X), I ⊆ irreducibleComponents X ∧ Set.range i = ⋃₀ I ∧ Set.range j = ⋃₀ (irreducibleComponents X \ I) ∧ (∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, topologicalKrullDim C = 1) ∧ ∃ e : Y ≅ (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (Closeds.closure ((Set.range j)ᶜ))).subscheme, e.hom ≫ (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (Closeds.closure ((Set.range j)ᶜ))).subschemeι = i
